## Overview

RISC-V custom instruction extensions are typically verified with constrained-random
tools (riscv-dv) or formal property checkers (OneSpin). Both approaches leave
coverage gaps: random simulation cannot prove absence of invalid encodings, and
formal tools require significant expertise to set up and maintain.

ev takes a different approach. Rather than sampling the encoding space or proving
properties about it, ev exhaustively enumerates every valid combination of
instruction fields, evaluates all constraints, and reports the result for every
single encoding. The answer is complete, deterministic, and reproducible.

## Approach

A declarative specification describes the instruction encoding space including
field ranges and cross-field constraints. The tool computes the Cartesian
product of all field domains, evaluates every point against the constraint set,
and projects each result through configurable projector functions. It is
architecture-agnostic and format-agnostic.

The extension model is trait-based, supporting new constraint types, projector
functions, input formats, and output formats without modifying the core
pipeline.

## Status

ev has been validated against real production RISC-V core interfaces and
demonstrates sub-minute exhaustive verification on industry-standard hardware
for specification spaces exceeding 33 million combinations. Independent
cross-verification against hand-written RISC-V assembly confirms deterministic
consistency across implementation substrates.

Current development focuses on expanding the constraint and projector library,
additional simulation backends, and integration with broader hardware
verification workflows.
